label: Live cross-path top-1 agreement is 19/20 comparable probes and the single divergence is stable: P7 returns sk-code 0.8899 on Python in 4/4 runs and system-spec-kit 0.8364 on Node in 4/4 runs; P1 agrees at sk-code 0.8787 once the Python path answers. A top-1 parity check has exactly one live disagreement on this battery, deterministic rather than flaky.

0.82 exact ties are common: 5 of 21 Python-scored probes (5 of 22 Node-scored) end with top-1 confidence exactly 0.82 and the runner-up also exactly 0.82 - P3, P5, P15, N1, N5; 11/21 have 0.82 anywhere in the top two (Node 10, missing P4). Roughly one in four probes is an exact floor tie, identically resolved on both paths.

Measured per-prompt cost: Python 1.76s mean (range 0.77-4.46s; 38.7s total over 21 calls) vs Node 0.59s mean (range 0.24-1.10s; 13.0s over 22 calls) - roughly 3x. For the 17+5 battery that is about 39s versus 13s end-to-end. Caveat: the Node daemon was pre-warmed (freshness live on every response), so cold-daemon start cost is unmeasured.

The first Python invocation failed transiently with NATIVE_CALL_FAILED (exit 2, native-unavailable, after 4.46s) and the same prompt then succeeded 3/3 on replay at sk-code 0.8787 (2.7-3.1s). A one-shot parity pass would record a false divergence; the existing battery's per-call exit-code check and degraded-run refusal is the precedent a gate must keep.

Live battery state passes on both paths: Node 15/17 positives (misses P4 to system-deep-loop, P7 to system-spec-kit) and Python 16/17 counting the P1 replay (15/16 on the primary pass); negatives 0/5 on both paths. P4 and P7 are the two probes out of scope for fixes, recorded as evidence only. The negative half only asserts sk-code avoidance: N3/N4/N5 do not match their stated expected top-1.

Measured confidence drift confirms the raw-confidence elimination: top-1 confidence is identical on 17/20 comparable probes, drifts slightly on 2 (P4 0.92 vs 0.9248; N3 0.95 vs 0.9459), and differs fully at P7 (0.8899 vs 0.8364). Comparing raw confidence would add two false diffs to the one real divergence; confidence belongs in the record, not the parity predicate.
A live parity pass over both advisor paths left the worktree unchanged: git status identical before/after and /tmp/system-skill-advisor entry count 20 -> 20
